themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.

hero.oneLiner: The deck positions Optiemus Infracom as an electronics manufacturing services (EMS) platform pivoting into proprietary B2C products, with growth built on "Six Building Blocks" - EMS scale-up led by the AI+ smartphone partnership, the MPMS/PLI 2.0 policy tailwind, screen protectors, a second B2C category, a Corning cover-glass JV and drones - targeting Rs 6,000 crore revenue by FY29.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Claims market leadership as "#1 in Hearables & Wearables in India - trusted by premium global brands", within a diversified platform spanning smartphones, hearables and wearables, fintech hardware, telecom and IoT modules.
- Describes a deliberately de-risked model: "Exited volatile local-brand contracts, onboarded premium customers, ensuring consistent volumes".
- Positions the smartphone win as a deep strategic relationship rather than a contract - "Strategic EMS partner to the brand", with the ramp called the "Largest single-program ramp in OEL's history".
- Cover glass is framed as a deep-tech moat: "Advanced material science - capital-intensive, with high entry barriers", executed through a 70:30 JV between Optiemus Infracom and Corning International Corp.
- Stated vision: "Leveraging our deep distribution expertise and world-class EMS capabilities, we aim to build a proprietary B2C product portfolio" - identifying products where in-house manufacturing and go-to-market strengths can be fully leveraged.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [JV] Cover glass is a 70:30 JV between Optiemus Infracom and Corning International Corp., branded "BIG Tech" in the deck.
- [Policy] Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (PLI 2.0) is a cabinet-approved Rs 62,500 crore scheme running FY27-FY31; the deck calls it a "STRUCTURAL GAME CHANGER FOR US" and claims first-mover advantage through the AI+ partnership and a "FIRST-MOVER TEMPLATE" to onboard other Indian brands.
- [Regulation] Mandatory BIS certification for screen protectors is expected by Jan '27 and is expected to restrict grey-market imports; the deck sizes the addressable screen protector market at ~Rs 20,000 cr today ("Market - Imports only") with Rs 40,000 cr potential by 2030, on 60 crore smartphone users in India at ~2 pieces per year average usage.
- [Guidance] FY27 revenue target of ~Rs 3,600 cr (~2x FY26 revenue), then 30%+ annual growth in FY28 and FY29 to a Rs 6,000 crore revenue target by FY29 - explicitly excluding any contribution from screen protectors, cover glass and the Q3 FY27 B2C launch, with drones as additional optionality.
- [Incubation and other income] Incubation expenses for the Drones and Cover Glass businesses impacted PAT by Rs 245 Lakhs in the quarter, with core operating PAT stated at Rs 2,363 Lakhs adjusting for these; separately, Other Income of Rs 1,091 lakhs was "primarily driven by ongoing government policy incentives (expected to be of recurring nature)".
